mqttSettings.ok: Connected in {{ms}} ms ({{transport}}). The settings work: remember to save them.
mqttSettings.fail_dns: The address “{{host}}” does not exist or DNS cannot find it.
mqttSettings.fail_refused: {{host}} answers, but there is no broker on port {{port}} (connection refused).
mqttSettings.fail_timeout: No answer from {{host}}:{{port}}: a firewall blocks the port, or the address is wrong.
mqttSettings.fail_tls: The broker wants different encryption: TLS failed or was not expected.
mqttSettings.fail_auth: The broker refused the user name or password.
mqttSettings.tls_hint: TLS is used automatically on port 8883. If the broker requires it on another port, use 8883.
mqttSettings.guide_title: How another system reads the data
mqttSettings.guide_desc: To connect a SCADA, Node-RED or a MES to OpenEdge's MQTT broker.
mqttSettings.guide_values_names: Names are lower case, with spaces, “_” and “/” turned into “-”.
mqttSettings.guide_payload_desc: v = value (already in engineering units if the tag is scaled), ts = milliseconds since 1970 (UTC), q = quality (0 = good).
mqttSettings.guide_sparkplug_desc: When publishing is set to Sparkplug (below), the same values also go out as Sparkplug B, with node birth and death.
mqttSettings.guide_access_desc: The broker requires a user name and password, and each organization receives only its own tags' data. Credentials for an external system (read-only) are created in Organizations → Infrastructure → MQTT.
mqttSettings.guide_monitor: Watch the messages live in the MQTT Monitor
